recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not add Encounter or Procedure to CarePlan.activity.plannedActivityReference. If SupplyRequest support is revisited, handle that through the later SupplyRequest/core-incubator issue family rather than FHIR-3077.
issue_request: FHIR-3077 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for DSTU1. It asked that CarePlan.activity.detail describe planned activities/orders rather than actual event resources, removing Encounter and Procedure and using appropriate order/request resources instead.
initial_application: No current git commit directly mentions FHIR-3077, consistent with early DSTU1 application. In current build-scoped source, CarePlan is active in source/fhir.ini, the historical CarePlan.activity.detail name maps to CarePlan.activity.plannedActivityReference, and the active plannedActivityReference target list omits Encounter and Procedure.
additional_context: Later CarePlan work preserved and clarified the same boundary. FHIR-26064 split requested/planned activity from performed event activity. FHIR-39101 removed the active inline plannedActivityDetail path and relied on plannedActivityReference for requested activity. FHIR-34477 added SupplyRequest to plannedActivityReference, but commit 3b38b80cf2 later removed SupplyRequest from core when OO resources moved to an incubator. FHIR-6349 separately rejected allowing activity references to any resource.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit was made because the current active CarePlan definition already implements the seed issue: plannedActivityReference lists request/planning targets and excludes Encounter and Procedure, while performedActivity is documented for event resources such as Encounter and Procedure. Old plannedActivityDetail source blocks, examples, and search parameters are commented out.

related_jiras.note: Split CarePlan planned activity references from performed event activity, confirming where Encounter and Procedure belong.
Removed the active inline plannedActivityDetail path and relied on plannedActivityReference for requested activities.

Rejected broad CarePlan activity references to any resource and reiterated that Encounter and Procedure are event resources handled elsewhere.
Added the separate CarePlan.encounter context element; it does not change the planned activity target set.
